hints: Look closely at compound Q and spot the key functional group that controls all of its reactions here.
Draw out Q as $\text{CH}_3\text{C}(\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3)=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and note which two groups are attached to each C of the C=C bond.
Recall how alkenes add $\text{Cl}_2$, $\text{Br}_2$ and cold $\text{MnO}_4^-$ across the double bond, and check whether each addition needs light for radicals or is ionic electrophilic.
walkthrough:
**Identify compound Q**

Q is a substituted alkene with an ester side chain. Write it clearly to see the double bond.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{C}(\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3)=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$$

**Recall alkene chemistry**

Alkenes undergo electrophilic addition across the C=C bond. The pi bond breaks and the two new atoms or groups add one to each C of the former double bond.

$$\text{>C=C< + X-Y} \rightarrow \text{>C(X)-C(Y)<}$$

**Check polymerisation**

Addition polymerisation just opens the double bond to a single bond, but the substituents stay on the same carbons. Q should give $-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)(\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}(\text{H})(\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3)-$ as the repeat unit, with $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$ together.

**Check addition of halogens and manganate(VII)**

With $\text{Cl}_2$ or $\text{Br}_2$ in the dark, the correct product is $\text{CH}_3\text{C}(\text{X})(\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}(\text{X})\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ by electrophilic addition, not free radical. Free radical substitution needs UV light and happens on alkanes. With cold, dilute acidified $\text{MnO}_4^-$, mild oxidation gives the diol by adding one OH to each C.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{C}(\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3)=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{C}(\text{OH})(\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}(\text{OH})\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$

**Conclude the correct statement**

Only the diol formation matches both the correct connectivity and the correct reagent and conditions. That is the correct description of Q.

options.A: Incorrect. Polymerisation keeps substituents on their original carbons. The left C of the C=C carries both $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$, so the repeat unit must be $-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)(\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}(\text{H})(\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3)-$. Option A swaps them to put $\text{H}$ with $\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$.
options.B: Incorrect on two counts. Addition of $\text{Cl}_2$ to an alkene is electrophilic addition, not free radical (free radical needs UV light and is typical of alkane substitution). The skeleton shown is also wrong, it moves $\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$ to the wrong carbon.
options.C: Correct. Cold, dilute acidified manganate(VII) gives mild oxidation (syn dihydroxylation) of the alkene. Each C of the C=C gains an OH, giving $\text{CH}_3\text{C}(\text{OH})(\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}(\text{OH})\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, exactly as shown with all groups in the right places.
options.D: Incorrect because of the mechanism. The connectivity $\text{CH}_3\text{C}(\text{Br})(\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}(\text{Br})\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ is the right product for addition of $\text{Br}_2$, but addition of bromine to an alkene is electrophilic addition, not free radical. Free radical is a trap linked to UV light conditions.
